instruction: I'm on Ubuntu. Please set LibreOffice Writer as my default word processor.

metadata.explanation: Task variation that sets LibreOffice Writer as the default word processor. Uses custom getter get_default_word_processor__d4070ff6 which checks the application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text MIME type handler using xdg-mime query. Evaluates that the default word processor includes 'libreoffice-writer.desktop'.
metadata.verification: The getter queries the default handler for application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text MIME type using xdg-mime. The metric check_include_exclude verifies that 'libreoffice-writer.desktop' appears in the result, confirming LibreOffice Writer is set as the default word processor.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification coverage: The getter only checks the MIME type 'application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text' (ODF .odt files), but a complete 'default word processor' verification should check multiple MIME types including .doc, .docx, .rtf, etc.

Semantic narrowness: The instruction asks to verify LibreOffice Writer as the 'default word processor' (system-wide for all word processing formats), but the evaluator only verifies one specific document format association
The technical implementation is correct and will work at runtime, but it provides incomplete verification of the instruction requirement
A user could have LibreOffice Writer set as default for .odt files but another application for .doc/.docx files, and this evaluator would incorrectly pass
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Extend the getter to check multiple MIME types: 'application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text', 'application/msword', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document', 'application/rtf'
Return a dictionary or list of MIME type associations and verify LibreOffice Writer is set for all common word processing formats
Alternative: Use xdg-settings to check the default application for text/plain or use x-scheme-handler/file associations
Update the metric to verify multiple MIME type associations, not just one
